title: Latency Sculptor — daily notes and triage
content:
Morning dump (walkthrough of last 36h):

- Symptom: intermittent p99 spikes on hosted inference for chat route (mistral-variant) during small concurrent bursts (~40-60 rps). p50/p90 stable, p99 jumps from ~230ms to ~1.6s for short windows of ~30-90s.
- Observed correlated signals: KV-cache hit-rate drops from ~95% -> ~60%; batching rate increases (more micro-batches), and one worker instance showed sustained GPU memory fragmentation warnings in logs.
- Alerts: infra-alert INF-4321 triggered twice; paging rotation went to Mina on second page.

Initial hypothesis/notes:
- KV cache eviction storm: suspect an eviction boundary bug where a single large request (long context) causes a cascade that invalidates shards aggressively, causing cache cold starts and extra decoding cost. The p99 aligns with warmup decode cost plus new KV fetch.
- Batching sensitives: when requests are too small but bursty, scheduler creates many tiny batches; continuous batching backlog is low but dispatch overhead is higher. Combined with frequent cache misses, tail latency compounds.
- Memory fragmentation: kernel allocator doing many small allocations (attention KV slices) causing fragmentation -> occasional copy-outs leading to stalls. Might match the worker logs (fragmentation warnings).

Quick repro plan (local / canary):
1) Repro script: replay real traffic snippet that triggered INF-4321 with original headers. Use replay-tool with tokenization-preserving mode. (TODO: extract trace from observability — get recording id from the alert).
2) Inject synthetic long-context request (len ~8k tokens) in a small burst to simulate eviction. Measure cache hit-rate and per-token latency.
3) Try toggles: a) KV-cache conservative eviction policy b) force quantized-kv-path c) disable continuous-batching for that route. Compare p99 across runs.

Commands/notes to run quickly:
- fetch traces: ./scripts/trace-fetch.sh INF-4321 --since 2026-03-08T00:00Z --out tmp/trace-4321.json
- replay: python tools/replay.py --trace tmp/trace-4321.json --mode token-preserve --concurrency 40 --target canary-3
- perf counters: nvprof and simple memstats snapshots on canary-3 during replay.

Immediate tasks (short):
- [ ] Pull the full trace and filter to long-context requests (Sanjay) — due today EOD.
- [ ] Add temporary route throttle (burst cap) for chat:mistral-variant on hosted to reduce burst surface (Priya) — coordinate with ops to avoid customer impact.
- [ ] Roll a canary with KV-cache policy fallback (conservative) and compare p99 (Mina + Sanjay).
- [ ] Reproduce locally with replay and confirm whether fragmentation log lines co-occur with spikes (Sanjay).

Longer-term investigations (notes / brainstorm):
- Eviction policy tuning: we should consider a sliding-window LRU that is sticky for small contexts and more aggressive for large contexts (long-request penalty). Current policy appears size-only and can thrash.
- Batching policy: adaptive micro-batch cutoffs based on recent inter-arrival times per-route. The scheduler currently uses global thresholds; per-route heuristics could reduce tiny-batch overhead.
- Memory allocator: evaluate jemalloc alternatives or tuning (tcache sizes, arena counts) for GPU-side allocator used by our attention kernels. If fragmentation confirmed, try coalesced allocation paths for KV buffers.
- Observability: need a KV-cache evictions metric exposed per-shard + eviction-causes tag (size-evict vs time-evict vs manual). Right now it's opaque.

Triage notes from Slack threads: 
- Priya: "saw a cluster of >1s p99 around 03:14 UTC; queues backed up; one node OOM-killed but restarted quickly"
- Mina: "can reproduce with a 6k token request mixed with many 20-60 token requests; disabling continuous-batching reduces p99 but costs throughput"
- Ops: recommended token-bucket limiter as quick mitigation for hosted tier; want to avoid breaking customer SLAs.

Edge cases found in quick code skim: 
- cache/shard_manager.cc line ~412: eviction loop uses `while (used_bytes > limit) pop_oldest()`; but pop_oldest has an early-return when encountering a 'pinned' item — this can leave used_bytes > limit and trigger another eviction pass that may clear multiple shards unexpectedly. Add a safeguard counter and logging.
- dispatcher/scheduler.py: per-route queue aging is globalized; the micro-batch flush condition uses global timeouts which misclassifies bursts with mixed sizes.

Hypothesis experiments (A/B):
A) ConservativeKV: change eviction threshold + disable large-object fast-path for 24h canary.
B) PerRouteBatching: enable per-route inter-arrival heuristic for chat routes on a small fleet.
C) AllocTune: jemalloc tcache reduce for worker container to see if fragmentation improves.

Metrics to collect (must add to dashboard):
- KV-cache hit-rate (per route, per-shard) 1m/30s granularity
- Eviction rate and eviction-cause histogram
- Batch size distribution and batch-dispatch latency histograms
- p50/p90/p99 per model variant and per-canary instance
- GPU allocator fragmentation metric (RSS vs allocator-reported used)

Meeting action items (short bullet updates for sync):
- Today 11:30am sync: quick demo of repro + expected mitigations. Bring canary logs + nvprof snapshots. (Priya leading)
- Postmortem owner assignment: Sanjay (draft) — due 3 days after incident close.

Random thoughts / heuristics to write down:
- "Favor stability over micro-ops" — in high tail situations, a small throughput hit (throttling, conservative eviction) buys 10x reduction in p99.
- Consider an explicit "long-request" tag at ingress so downstream cache/batching can treat it differently rather than inferring from size.

Open questions:
- Are there recent merges that changed eviction semantics? (check PRs merged in last 7 days affecting cache/shard_manager).
- Does the canary fleet run the exact same jemalloc build as prod? Small allocator build differences can show up only at scale.

Notes to self (todo when calm):
- Add small logging patch to shard_manager to emit eviction-cause and pinned-count every 1000 evictions. Keep it low-overhead.
- Add a lightweight per-route batching metric to the request pipeline; it can be a counter + moving average of inter-arrival times.
- Draft a small customer-facing blurb for CSE explaining temporary burst caps if ops ask to communicate.

End of dump. Will iterate on repro steps after trace fetch.

-- Sanjay

(If you're reading this in future: look at tmp/trace-4321.json, replay results in tmp/replay-4321/*.log, and top-line comparison CSV tmp/repro-summary.csv)
